name: RTX
description: RTX makes aircraft engines, aircraft systems and missiles and sensors. Pratt & Whitney sells engines new and then earns recurring aftermarket revenue servicing them over decades; Collins Aerospace makes cockpit, power, interior and actuation systems and sells original equipment and spares; Raytheon builds missiles, air defense, radars and effectors mainly for the US and allied governments. Roughly half of 2025 sales (48 percent) were commercial aerospace and other commercial customers, and about 38 percent went to the US government; backlog reached $268 billion at the end of 2025 (commercial $161 billion, defense $107 billion). Its commercial side is the aerospace aftermarket cycle, and Pratt's Geared Turbofan fleet inspections (Powder Metal Matter) are a continuing cost.

employees.note: Approximately 180,000 employees, about 54,000 of them engineers and about 32,000 union or works-council represented.

businessLines.name: Collins Aerospace
businessLines.how: Sells aerospace systems (avionics, power, interiors, actuation, mission systems) to aircraft makers as original equipment, then spare parts and service to airlines over the life of the aircraft, plus defense programmes; 68 percent of its 2025 external sales were to commercial customers (18,858 of 27,585, computed).

businessLines.name: Pratt & Whitney
businessLines.how: Sells large commercial and military aircraft engines (including the Geared Turbofan family powering more than 2,600 aircraft) at thin original-equipment margins, then earns recurring aftermarket revenue from parts, repair and long-term service on the installed fleet; 2025 sales growth was driven by commercial aftermarket (+$2.9 billion).

businessLines.name: Raytheon
businessLines.how: Sells missiles, air and missile defense, radars, sensors and effectors to the US government and allied governments under multi-year fixed-price and cost-plus contracts; revenue follows production and delivery of awarded programmes.

brands.name: Pratt & Whitney Geared Turbofan (PW1000G) family
brands.note: Powers more than 2,600 aircraft for more than 90 operators (A320neo family, A220, Embraer E-Jets E2); GTF Advantage engine certified by FAA and EASA in 2025
